title: Define Hook, Request, and Token data models
user_story: As a developer, I need well-typed data models for hooks, captured requests, and auth tokens so the rest of the codebase can pass structured data instead of raw strings.
description: Define the core domain types from CLAUDE.md: Hook (a named webhook inbox), Request (a captured HTTP request), and Token (optional auth). These are plain structs with serde Serialize/Deserialize. IDs use nanoid for hooks and UUID v4 for requests. Include Display and test coverage.

acceptance_criteria.then: it has a nanoid hook_id, a name, created_at timestamp, and request_count field
it stores request_id (UUID v4), hook_id, method, url path, headers (as JSON), body (bytes), content_length, source IP, and received_at timestamp
it has a token_id, hook_id (optional — can be global), created_at, and expires_at
serde produces the expected fields with snake_case naming
tests verify creation, serialization round-trip, and field constraints

functions.name: Hook::new
functions.description: Create a new hook with generated nanoid

functions.name: CapturedRequest::new
functions.signature: pub fn new(hook_id: &str, method: &str, path: &str, headers: HeaderMap, body: Vec<u8>, source_ip: IpAddr) -> CapturedRequest
functions.description: Create a new captured request with generated UUID

single_binary_checklist.notes: Pure data types. nanoid and uuid are small crates with no system deps.
